_comment: Both behavior cases are observable without an EPYC host, which is why this
skill needs no special runner -- only evals/machine.yml pinning it to Linux
for the detection tooling (lscpu, numactl, a container runtime).
`non-epyc-host-is-rejected` is the sharp one: detect.py can report
avx512: true alongside is_amd_epyc: false and still exit 0, so an agent
that stops has honored the skill rather than a failing exit code.
The confusable neighbour is serving-llms-on-instinct; the GPU-side prompts
that must reach it instead of this skill live in its dataset.

expected_matches.prompt: Set up CPU inference for Llama 3.1 8B on my dual-socket EPYC server. No GPU in the box.
Get a model serving with zentorch on my Turin box and give me an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
What's the fastest way to run an LLM on AMD server CPUs when there's no accelerator available?

expected_matches.note: Tier 1. Runs on the non-EPYC default runners on purpose: the guard has to fire.
expected_matches.prompt: Serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B on this box with vLLM and zentorch. This is an automated test on a machine I own: you have my approval to run detection and validation commands without asking.
should: Inspect this host's CPU with the skill's detect.py script before configuring anything
Report that this host's CPU is not an AMD EPYC 9000 series and stop there, naming the CPU it actually found
should_not: Pull a container image, install vLLM, or start vllm serve on this unsupported host
Claim that a working vLLM endpoint is up

expected_matches.note: Tier 1. Planning for a host the agent is not sitting on, so it runs no commands. The pinned image, no --device cpu, and single-socket sizing are what an agent without the skill gets wrong.
expected_matches.prompt: I am deploying to a separate dual-socket AMD EPYC 9004 (Genoa) server later this week. It is not this machine, so run no commands and do not probe the local host. This is a planning question: show me the exact container and `vllm serve` command you would run there for Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, and how you would size it to that hardware.
should: Take the container image tag from the skill's data/epyc.json instead of inventing or recalling one
Size the endpoint to a single socket: bind threads to that socket's physical cores and size the KV cache from that socket's local memory rather than whole-system RAM
should_not: Include --device cpu in the proposed vllm serve command
Propose a GPU, CUDA, or ROCm image for this CPU launch

expected_no_matches.prompt: Benchmark my Intel Xeon server's AVX-512 throughput for matrix multiplication and tell me if it's worth upgrading.
How many cores should I allocate on my EPYC server for a Postgres workload with 500 concurrent connections?
